title: VisionCreator-R1: A Reflection-Enhanced Native Visual-Generation Agentic Model
claim: Agents without reflection or with under- or over-reflection yield wrong outputs; good reflection detects errors and repairs them to reach the right result.
layout: Query panel left, image trajectory center-right, failure branches above, color-coded boxes
description: A gray query box on the left describes a gallery scene with an art critic, a collector and a young artist. Next to it is the first generated image, which shows only two people. Along the top, arrows lead from this image to a gray 'without-Reflection' box and on to an orange 'Undesired Answer ✗' box. A blue 'Redundant Repair' box sits at the top right. Below the top row, an orange-tinted 'Under-Reflection: Accept' box and a blue 'Over-Reflection: Reject' box mark the other failure modes. The main trajectory sits in a green outlined region. 'Good-Reflection: Reject' boxes drive two repair steps with image2image_tool. The images improve from two people, to three people with the wrong person pointing, to the correct scene. It ends in an orange 'Desired Answer ✓' box. Green, orange and blue boxes separate the reflection types.
caption: Comparison between without-Reflection, with {Good-Reflection}, Under-Reflection and Over-Reflection.
abstract: Visual content generation has advanced from single-image to multi-image workflows, yet existing agents remain largely plan-driven and lack systematic reflection mechanisms to correct mid-trajectory visual errors. To address this limitation, we propose VisionCreator-R1, a native visual generation agent with explicit reflection, together with a Reflection-Plan Co-Optimization (RPCO) training methodology. Through extensive experiments and trajectory-level analysis, we uncover reflection-plan optimization asymmetry in reinforcement learning (RL): planning can be reliably optimized via plan rewards, while reflection learning is hindered by noisy credit assignment. Guided by this insight, our RPCO first trains on the self-constructed VCR-SFT dataset with reflection-strong single-image trajectories and planning-strong multi-image trajectories, then co-optimization on VCR-RL dataset via RL. This yields our unified VisionCreator-R1 agent, which consistently outperforms Gemini2.5Pro on existing benchmarks and our VCR-bench covering single-image and multi-image tasks.
